Section 1: Executive Summary & Operating Reality

1. Business Model Reality & Core Moat Analysis

StoneCo Ltd. (NASDAQ: STNE) has completed a structural strategic transformation, divesting non-core software assets to refine its operational focus strictly on its high-return financial technology flywheel. The company operates a fully integrated ecosystem designed specifically for Brazilian Micro, Small, and Medium Businesses (MSMBs), generating recurring cash flows across three interconnected pillars: Merchant Acquiring & Payments, Digital Banking, and MSMB Credit Solutions.

Strategic Refocusing & Capital Allocation Event: On February 20, 2026, StoneCo formally closed the sale of Linx to TOTVS for an enterprise value of R$3.05 billion. Retaining roughly R$3.8 billion in amortizable fiscal goodwill, management promptly returned the net proceeds via a landmark extraordinary dividend of $2.53 per share (~R$3.08 billion total) on May 4, 2026. Former CEO and Board Chairman Pedro Zinner summarized the rationale: "Our competitive advantages live at a very specific intersection: payments, banking, and credit... Linx was a good business sitting outside that intersection."

Revenue Generation & Ecosystem Economics

StoneCo’s fundamental thesis relies on deep monetization of merchant cash flows through proprietary distribution channels (Hubs) and end-to-end technology:

  • Merchant Acquiring (Payments): Stone earns transaction processing fees (take rate) on Total Payment Volume (TPV), augmented by pre-payment fees (receivables discounting/antecipação). While card TPV expansion has moderated to single digits due to macroeconomic tightness, PIX QR code payment volumes have surged, offering lower headline take rates but significantly higher customer engagement and lower funding costs.
  • Digital Banking Services: StoneCo functions as the primary operational bank for over 2 million merchants. Revenue is generated via interest income on retail deposits (R$10.1 billion balance), account maintenance, wire fees, and interchange on business debit/credit cards. Banking deposits serve as a low-cost internal funding base for credit operations.
  • MSMB Credit Solutions: Leveraging real-time POS transaction data, Stone underwrites working capital loans and credit cards. Credit generates elevated gross yields (credit revenue reached R$297 million in Q1 2026), with repayments automatically deducted directly from daily merchant acquiring settlements.

Pricing Power, Take-Rate Trends & Customer Retention

StoneCo's structural competitive moat—historically anchored by its hyper-local sales Hubs and superior customer service—faced friction following aggressive pricing adjustments implemented during 2024–2025 to offset elevated domestic interest rates (Selic). While these repricing initiatives initially protected net interest margins, they triggered client churn among fee-sensitive 2025 merchant cohorts and caused a temporary contraction in active clients. Management is currently shifting focus from pure client volume to maximizing Average Revenue Per Active Client (ARPAC) through bundled payments, banking, and credit integration.

2. Recent Performance & Operational Execution

For Q1 2026, StoneCo delivered mixed operational results characterized by steady top-line growth and disciplined share buybacks, offset by escalating credit provisions and margin pressure.

Top-line revenue expanded to R$3.58 billion, underpinned by credit portfolio expansion (+14% QoQ to R$3.2 billion) and stable merchant acquiring performance. Adjusted Basic EPS grew 15.0% YoY to R$2.19 (~$0.42 USD equivalent), outstripping net income growth due to aggressive equity repurchases. Year-to-date capital returned to shareholders reached R$3.6 billion (including the Linx extraordinary dividend and R$600 million in ordinary share buybacks), with an additional R$1.4 billion committed for buybacks through year-end 2026.

Credit Deterioration & Operational Execution Stress

The primary earnings drag in Q1 2026 stemmed from accelerating credit losses within micro and small business portfolios, driven by persistent high Selic interest rates (~10.5%–12.0%) in Brazil:

  • Surging Provision Costs: Adjusted gross profit remained flat at R$1.50 billion as top-line gains were fully offset by a >50% QoQ surge in expected credit loss provisions. Cost of Risk escalated sharply to 21.9%.
  • NPL Spike: Non-performing loans (90+ day NPLs) expanded toward 7.0%, reflecting acute debt-servicing stress among smaller merchants.
  • Client Base Purge & Churn: The active client base decreased 5% sequentially to 4.7 million. This reduction reflected both management’s deliberate purging of low-engagement, unprofitable accounts and elevated churn within 2025 cohorts impacted by post-repricing friction.
Management Strategy to Remediate Churn & Credit Stress:

Heading into the Q2 2026 reporting period (scheduled for August 13, 2026), executive management has reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance, projecting gross profit and net income acceleration in 2H 2026. To mitigate churn and control credit risk, StoneCo is executing a three-part turnaround strategy:

  1. Pricing Simplification & Transparent Bundling: Unifying payments and banking fees into transparent, fixed-tier packages to reduce merchant billing friction.
  2. Dedicated Account Management Desks: Re-engaging high-ARPAC merchants via localized Hub incentives and specialized retention desks.
  3. Pivot to Secured Credit Underwriting: Pivoting new credit origination away from uncollateralized working capital loans toward secured, collateralized lending products and credit card solutions to structurally curb NPL formation.

Section 3: Real Cash Flow Generation, SBC & Float Discipline

Evaluating StoneCo’s true earning capacity requires looking past GAAP accounting and digging directly into cash conversion, stock compensation dilution, and working capital dynamics. In payments and banking platforms, reported Operating Cash Flow (OCF) is often distorted by short-term working capital fluctuations, merchant prepayment receivables (ARV), and merchant payables settlement timing.

Warren Buffett Owner Earnings & SBC Adjustments

In accordance with fundamental owner-earnings principles, Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) is treated as a 100% real economic expense and a direct cause of shareholder dilution. While accounting standards add back SBC to operating cash flows as a non-cash item, issuing shares to executives dilutes existing owners' equity claims just as real cash wages do. Additionally, total capital expenditures are separated into Maintenance CapEx (the capital needed to replace aging POS terminals and preserve software infrastructure) and Growth CapEx (investments to expand into credit and banking solutions).

Float Discipline & Cost of Funding Advantage: StoneCo operates an organic customer float engine. By consolidating merchant acquiring, payments, and digital banking accounts, client deposits grew significantly in Q1 2026, reducing overall funding costs to 87% of CDI (down from 100% in early 2025). This interest-free and low-cost customer float provides a key operational funding cushion, shielding net interest margins (NIM) even during periods of elevated central bank interest rates.

Section 4: Balance Sheet Reality, Capital Allocation & Ownership

StoneCo’s capital allocation strategy underwent a structural reset following the divestment of its Linx software division. The transaction freed up capital, enabling management to clear legacy operational sprawl, bolster balance sheet cash reserves, and execute large capital returns through extraordinary dividends and share repurchases.

Capital Allocation Takeaway: Management has demonstrated a commitment to returning excess capital. By pairing the US$2.53 per share (R$3.08B) extraordinary dividend with an aggressive share buyback program (repurchasing over 29 million shares under its R$2.0B authorization), StoneCo is systematically shrinking its share count. This reduction helps offset the dilutive effects of executive Stock-Based Compensation (including the newly added 3.8 million share LTIP pool) while concentrating future Owner Earnings per share.

Section 5: Warren Buffett Owner Earnings & Intrinsic Valuation Matrix

To value StoneCo Ltd. (STNE) accurately, we apply Warren Buffett's 7-Pillar Intrinsic Value Framework as detailed in Berkshire Hathaway's shareholder letters. Market multiples and exit multiples are deliberately set aside to avoid relying on market sentiment. Instead, valuation is anchored in organic cash generation, capital efficiency, share count dynamics, and localized country-specific sovereign hurdle rates.

1. Normalized Owner Earnings Derivation

Under Buffett's 1986 formulation, Owner Earnings = Operating Cash Flow - Maintenance CapEx - Stock-Based Compensation (SBC). For StoneCo, Operating Cash Flow reflects true organic cash collected from merchant transaction processing and digital banking deposits, rather than short-term working capital timing spikes. Maintenance CapEx is strictly isolated to essential POS terminal replacements and core IT server maintenance, separating discretionary software growth CapEx. Stock-Based Compensation is deducted at 100% as a real economic expense that dilute existing equity owners.

On a capital-light Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) exceeding 30%, this high starting cash yield provides a substantial safety buffer, provided credit losses remain contained.

2. Localized Sovereign Discounting & Buyback Cannibal Dynamics

In accordance with Buffett’s cross-border capital allocation rules (e.g., PetroChina, Iscar), international businesses must never be discounted using US 10-Year Treasury rates. StoneCo’s cash flows are generated in Brazilian Reais (BRL) and are exposed to domestic macro volatility. Consequently, the discount rate is directly anchored to the local Brazilian NTN-F 10-Year Sovereign Bond Yield (~14.57%) plus an equity risk premium of 2.0% to 3.5%, establishing a baseline discount hurdle of 16.5% to 18.0%.

Simultaneously, management’s aggressive share repurchase strategy (including the R$5.0 billion buyback framework) serves as a key value driver. By retiring shares at deep discounts below intrinsic value, per-share Owner Earnings compound faster than top-line transaction volume.

Section 6: Thesis Confidence, Execution Risk & Pre-Mortem Falsification

Primary Thesis Conviction: Moderate Conviction
While StoneCo trades at a significant discount to its Base Case intrinsic value ($16.85) and provides a 23.0% starting Owner Earnings yield, overall conviction is capped at 'Moderate' due to macroeconomic sensitivity in Brazil, elevated credit loss provisions in the micro-merchant portfolio, and persistent double-digit sovereign funding costs.

Key Execution Risks & Vulnerabilities

The path to realizing intrinsic fair value faces three structural execution risks that require ongoing monitoring:

  • 1. Micro-Merchant Credit Defaults & Provision Escalation: As StoneCo expands its working capital loan book to MSMEs, credit default rates remain the primary tail risk. In Q1 2026, increased credit loss provisions compressed gross profit margins from 44.4% to 41.6%. Higher provisions could offset payment processing gains if underwriting models miscalculate default risk during economic slowdowns.
  • 2. High SELIC Persistence & Funding Cost Compression: With the Central Bank of Brazil (Copom) maintaining the benchmark SELIC rate at 14.0%–14.25%, high interest rates increase funding costs on liquidity lines used to finance prepayment transactions (FIDC). Prolonged double-digit interest rates limit net interest margin (NIM) expansion on merchant banking deposits.
  • 3. Price Competition & Take-Rate Compression: Aggressive pricing from incumbent acquiring networks (Itaú/Rede, Bradesco/Cielo) and fintech competitors (PagSeguro, Mercado Pago) poses an ongoing risk to merchant take-rates. Furthermore, the rapid adoption of Brazil's central bank instant payment system (Pix) reduces reliance on traditional debit cards.

Pre-Mortem Falsification Triggers

The following pre-defined quantitative and qualitative triggers would invalidate the investment thesis, requiring an immediate thesis downgrade or position exit:

Trigger 1: Non-Performing Loans (NPL 90+) Exceeding 6.0% of Credit Portfolio
If 90+ day non-performing loan ratios in the credit portfolio climb above 6.0% for two consecutive quarters, indicating systemic underwriting failures similar to the 2021 credit pause, the investment thesis is falsified.
Trigger 2: Normalized Gross Profit Margin Compression Below 38.0%
If gross profit margins drop below 38.0% (down from 41.6% in Q1 2026) due to take-rate erosion or elevated funding costs, it would signal structural margin degradation and invalidation of the capital-light moat hypothesis.
Trigger 3: Abandonment or Dilution of Share Buyback Execution
If management halts share repurchases despite the stock trading below book value ($9.65/share) or issues accretive stock-based compensation exceeding 3.5% of total share count annually, the cannibal compounding thesis is invalidated.

Section 1: Business Model, Scale Moat & GenAI Transition

StoneCo Ltd. (NASDAQ: STNE) operates Brazil's premier micro, small, and medium business (MSMB) financial operating system. Following the successful divestiture of its Linx enterprise software unit to Totvs for R$ 3.05 billion and the subsequent distribution of an extraordinary cash dividend of $2.53 per share in May 2026, StoneCo has successfully completed its strategic pivot back to a focused, capital-light fintech compounder. The company now commands an integrated triumvirate of merchant acquiring, digital banking, and secured/working-capital credit solutions across 4.8 million active business clients.

The core economic moat rests on StoneCo's proprietary "Stone Hub" distribution architecture, hyper-localized customer service ("Green Angels"), and a sticky merchant deposit base that grew to over R$ 10.1 billion. By securing a full Brazilian banking license, StoneCo has structurally decoupled its cost of funding from commercial bank wholesale lines, capturing zero-cost and low-cost merchant transaction float. This float provides a decisive cost of capital advantage over legacy acquirers and pure-play hardware vendors.

First-Principles Moat Dynamics: In payment acquiring, terminal hardware is a commodity, but localized software integrations, automated receivables anticipation, and low-cost deposit gathering create powerful negative-working-capital float. StoneCo captures merchant transaction flows at point-of-sale, providing instant visibility into borrower real-time revenues and providing automated daily loan collection directly at settlement.

On the operational efficiency frontier, StoneCo has completed the initial deployment of its proprietary GenAI merchant co-pilot and automated underwriting stack. By feeding multi-year point-of-sale transaction velocity and seasonal cash inflow data into real-time credit models, StoneCo is tightening its pre-approved credit disbursement limits while automating customer service routing across hubs, reducing servicing costs per active client by 4.2% YoY.

Section 2: Quarterly Operational Breakdown & Segment Performance

StoneCo's Q2 2026 financial release reflected resilient per-share bottom-line execution amidst a challenging macroeconomic tape characterized by sustained 14.00%–15.00% Brazilian SELIC benchmark interest rates. While headline revenue slightly missed consensus due to conservative acquiring take-rate adjustments on large accounts, profitability per share expanded steadily.

Section 6: Thesis Confidence, Execution Risk & Invalidation Corridors

Our thesis confidence is rated as Solid Conviction. The margin of safety is structurally wide: Mr. Market is pricing StoneCo as an impaired, high-delinquency credit trap at ~5.2x earnings, completely disregarding the fact that 26.3% Tier 1 capital and an ongoing R$ 2.0B buyback authorization insulate per-share value while management shifts toward collateralized MSMB credit.

Pre-Mortem Thesis Invalidation Corridors:
  • Credit Contagion Trigger: If NPL 90+ days accelerates past 11.0% and quarterly credit provisions exceed R$ 260M, indicating systemic underwriting failure rather than normal vintage seasoning.
  • Capital Misallocation Trigger: If management halts share buybacks below $12.00 to pursue speculative, dilutive cross-border M&A.
  • Take-Rate Collapse: If MSMB client churn exceeds 2.5% quarterly and acquiring take-rates compress by more than 20 bps due to predatory pricing by Itaú/Rede or Cielo.

StoneCo has navigated its major corporate restructuring, shed the distracting Linx software unit, delivered a major cash windfall to owners, and refocused on its core merchant operating franchise. We maintain a high-conviction BUY signal, recommending continued capital accumulation at current market quotations.

Section 1: Business Model, Scale Moat & GenAI Transition

StoneCo Ltd. operates as one of Brazil's preeminent financial technology ecosystems, serving micro, small, and medium-sized businesses (MSMBs) through an integrated offering spanning payments, digital banking, working capital credit, and business management software. Founded to disrupt Brazil's legacy banking oligopoly, StoneCo combines high-touch localized distribution ("StoneHubs") with proprietary cloud infrastructure and a white-glove customer service model.

The company's competitive moat is anchored in three core structural pillars:

  • Hyper-Local Distribution Advantage: Stone's proprietary Hub network delivers localized customer onboarding, physical terminal swap-outs within hours, and dedicated relationship managers—creating superior merchant retention compared to legacy bank branches.
  • Cross-Selling Velocity & Sticky Customer Float: StoneCo has successfully transitioned from a pure merchant discount rate (MDR) acquirer into a complete banking platform. Active banking clients generate low-cost deposit balances (R$6.5B+ float) that lower funding costs and power high-margin working capital lending.
  • GenAI Operational Automation: Management has deployed AI-driven credit underwriting algorithms, automated risk assessment, and AI-powered merchant dispute resolution. This transition is systematically driving operating leverage, allowing StoneCo to scale transaction volumes without linear headcount additions.
Warren Buffett 5-Year Market Closure Perspective: If the Nasdaq and B3 exchanges were shuttered for the next 5 years, StoneCo would remain an entrenched cash-printing machine in the Brazilian commercial landscape. Its sticky MSMB merchant relationships, high recurring software and banking float, and double-digit return on equity (21.6% ROE) ensure that internal capital compounding continues unimpeded by Mr. Market's daily quotations.

Section 4: Capital Allocation & Balance Sheet Discipline

StoneCo continues to execute one of the most aggressive "share cannibal" capital return programs in the global fintech sector.

  • Share Buyback Aggression: Over the trailing 12 months, StoneCo repurchased and retired 40.3 million Class A shares for ~R$3.0B (~$545M), shrinking the total diluted share base by ~14%. This aggressive share retirement allowed Adjusted EPS to expand +8.6% YoY even as consolidated net income remained flat.
  • Extraordinary Dividend Execution: StoneCo returned $2.53 per share (R$3.08B) via an extraordinary cash dividend in early 2026, realigning its capital structure while preserving a robust liquidity buffer.
  • Fortress Capital Position: Adjusted net cash stands at $245.5M (R$1,350.0M), while the managerial Tier 1 capital ratio for the prudential conglomerate remains at 26.3%—more than double the regulatory requirements set by the Brazilian Central Bank.
The Charlie Munger Cannibal Rule: When a high-return business buys back its own stock at 5.2x forward earnings and an 18.8% Owner Earnings yield, every dollar spent creates massive value for remaining owners. Each remaining share immediately claims a larger percentage of future corporate earnings.

Section 6: Thesis Confidence, Execution Risk & Invalidation Corridors

Our overall thesis confidence is ranked as Solid Conviction. The path to value realization is underpinned by tangible per-share cash flow growth, relentless share cannibalization, and a fortress balance sheet.

Key Execution Risks & Pre-Mortem Audit:

  • Credit Deterioration & NPL Spike: If 90+ day NPLs surge above 12.0% without adequate collateral recovery through receivables lockboxes, credit provisioning will consume operating profits.
  • Brazilian Macro / SELIC Rate Squeeze: Prolonged high interest rates in Brazil increase Stone's client funding costs and pressure MSMB merchant solvency.
  • Competitive Price Wars: Intensified merchant acquiring competition from PagBank, Cielo, or Rede could compress take-rates.

Thesis Invalidation Triggers (Immediate Exit / Downgrade Thresholds):

  • Trigger 1: Tier 1 Prudential Capital ratio drops below 16.0% due to unexpected credit book write-offs.
  • Trigger 2: Annual Owner Earnings fall below $350M sustainably.
  • Trigger 3: Share buyback program is canceled in favor of value-destructive, overpriced M&A.
Surveillance Corridor:
  • Upper Threshold ($15.50): Re-evaluate thesis as stock approaches Base Case fair value; begin systematic profit trimming.
  • Lower Threshold ($8.50): Urgent margin-of-safety review; inspect credit loss developments to determine if the bear case is materializing.

Section 1: Executive Summary & Operating Reality

1. Business Model Reality & Core Moat Analysis

StoneCo Ltd. (NASDAQ: STNE) has completed a structural strategic transformation, divesting non-core software assets to refine its operational focus strictly on its high-return financial technology flywheel. The company operates a fully integrated ecosystem designed specifically for Brazilian Micro, Small, and Medium Businesses (MSMBs), generating recurring cash flows across three interconnected pillars: Merchant Acquiring & Payments, Digital Banking, and MSMB Credit Solutions.

Strategic Refocusing & Capital Allocation Event: On February 20, 2026, StoneCo formally closed the sale of Linx to TOTVS for an enterprise value of R$3.05 billion. Retaining roughly R$3.8 billion in amortizable fiscal goodwill, management promptly returned the net proceeds via a landmark extraordinary dividend of $2.53 per share (~R$3.08 billion total) on May 4, 2026. Former CEO and Board Chairman Pedro Zinner summarized the rationale: "Our competitive advantages live at a very specific intersection: payments, banking, and credit... Linx was a good business sitting outside that intersection."

Revenue Generation & Ecosystem Economics

StoneCo’s fundamental thesis relies on deep monetization of merchant cash flows through proprietary distribution channels (Hubs) and end-to-end technology:

  • Merchant Acquiring (Payments): Stone earns transaction processing fees (take rate) on Total Payment Volume (TPV), augmented by pre-payment fees (receivables discounting/antecipação). While card TPV expansion has moderated to single digits due to macroeconomic tightness, PIX QR code payment volumes have surged, offering lower headline take rates but significantly higher customer engagement and lower funding costs.
  • Digital Banking Services: StoneCo functions as the primary operational bank for over 2 million merchants. Revenue is generated via interest income on retail deposits (R$10.1 billion balance), account maintenance, wire fees, and interchange on business debit/credit cards. Banking deposits serve as a low-cost internal funding base for credit operations.
  • MSMB Credit Solutions: Leveraging real-time POS transaction data, Stone underwrites working capital loans and credit cards. Credit generates elevated gross yields (credit revenue reached R$297 million in Q1 2026), with repayments automatically deducted directly from daily merchant acquiring settlements.

Pricing Power, Take-Rate Trends & Customer Retention

StoneCo's structural competitive moat—historically anchored by its hyper-local sales Hubs and superior customer service—faced friction following aggressive pricing adjustments implemented during 2024–2025 to offset elevated domestic interest rates (Selic). While these repricing initiatives initially protected net interest margins, they triggered client churn among fee-sensitive 2025 merchant cohorts and caused a temporary contraction in active clients. Management is currently shifting focus from pure client volume to maximizing Average Revenue Per Active Client (ARPAC) through bundled payments, banking, and credit integration.

Credit Deterioration & Operational Execution Stress

The primary earnings drag in Q1 2026 stemmed from accelerating credit losses within micro and small business portfolios, driven by persistent high Selic interest rates (~10.5%–12.0%) in Brazil:

  • Surging Provision Costs: Adjusted gross profit remained flat at R$1.50 billion as top-line gains were fully offset by a >50% QoQ surge in expected credit loss provisions. Cost of Risk escalated sharply to 21.9%.
  • NPL Spike: Non-performing loans (90+ day NPLs) expanded toward 7.0%, reflecting acute debt-servicing stress among smaller merchants.
  • Client Base Purge & Churn: The active client base decreased 5% sequentially to 4.7 million. This reduction reflected both management’s deliberate purging of low-engagement, unprofitable accounts and elevated churn within 2025 cohorts impacted by post-repricing friction.
Management Strategy to Remediate Churn & Credit Stress:

Heading into the Q2 2026 reporting period (scheduled for August 13, 2026), executive management has reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance, projecting gross profit and net income acceleration in 2H 2026. To mitigate churn and control credit risk, StoneCo is executing a three-part turnaround strategy:

  1. Pricing Simplification & Transparent Bundling: Unifying payments and banking fees into transparent, fixed-tier packages to reduce merchant billing friction.
  2. Dedicated Account Management Desks: Re-engaging high-ARPAC merchants via localized Hub incentives and specialized retention desks.
  3. Pivot to Secured Credit Underwriting: Pivoting new credit origination away from uncollateralized working capital loans toward secured, collateralized lending products and credit card solutions to structurally curb NPL formation.

The path to realizing intrinsic fair value faces three structural execution risks that require ongoing monitoring:

  • 1. Micro-Merchant Credit Defaults & Provision Escalation: As StoneCo expands its working capital loan book to MSMEs, credit default rates remain the primary tail risk. In Q1 2026, increased credit loss provisions compressed gross profit margins from 44.4% to 41.6%. Higher provisions could offset payment processing gains if underwriting models miscalculate default risk during economic slowdowns.
  • 2. High SELIC Persistence & Funding Cost Compression: With the Central Bank of Brazil (Copom) maintaining the benchmark SELIC rate at 14.0%–14.25%, high interest rates increase funding costs on liquidity lines used to finance prepayment transactions (FIDC). Prolonged double-digit interest rates limit net interest margin (NIM) expansion on merchant banking deposits.
  • 3. Price Competition & Take-Rate Compression: Aggressive pricing from incumbent acquiring networks (Itaú/Rede, Bradesco/Cielo) and fintech competitors (PagSeguro, Mercado Pago) poses an ongoing risk to merchant take-rates. Furthermore, the rapid adoption of Brazil's central bank instant payment system (Pix) reduces reliance on traditional debit cards.

Pre-Mortem Falsification Triggers

The following pre-defined quantitative and qualitative triggers would invalidate the investment thesis, requiring an immediate thesis downgrade or position exit:

Trigger 1: Non-Performing Loans (NPL 90+) Exceeding 6.0% of Credit Portfolio
If 90+ day non-performing loan ratios in the credit portfolio climb above 6.0% for two consecutive quarters, indicating systemic underwriting failures similar to the 2021 credit pause, the investment thesis is falsified.
Trigger 2: Normalized Gross Profit Margin Compression Below 38.0%
If gross profit margins drop below 38.0% (down from 41.6% in Q1 2026) due to take-rate erosion or elevated funding costs, it would signal structural margin degradation and invalidation of the capital-light moat hypothesis.
Trigger 3: Abandonment or Dilution of Share Buyback Execution
If management halts share repurchases despite the stock trading below book value ($9.65/share) or issues accretive stock-based compensation exceeding 3.5% of total share count annually, the cannibal compounding thesis is invalidated.
